task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-10-06, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
A defense's effect on opponents' H2-H1 change is a reliable team trait.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 120 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: defensive suppression of opponent H2-H1 change
defense as a reliable team trait
team-level defensive effect persistence across seasons
methodological_questions: Is a team-level defensive effect on opponent H2-H1 change reliable, measured by split-half or year-over-year stability?
How many team-seasons are needed to detect a stable defensive trait?
Do regression to the mean or selection bias inflate apparent defensive persistence?
How should H2-H1 change be measured to limit score-state, pace and opponent-quality confounding?
evidence_establishes: No earlier study by this project was returned for this question, its concepts or its methods, so no prior finding on defensive H2-H1 reliability is established by the retrieval.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether opponent H2-H1 change is a reliable team defensive trait.
Whether any earlier project test of this question exists, was run, or failed.
What power, reliability or effect-size benchmarks apply to this measure.
Whether the derived play-type graph records or the matchup-minute files are validated for this use.
own_inferences: The stated unit count of 120 equals 4 regular seasons (2022-23 to 2025-26) x 30 teams, so the primary sample is the full regular-season population with no room for extra team-seasons; playoffs add small, unequal samples.

Year-over-year pairs give about 90 team pairs (3 consecutive season pairs x 30 teams), which limits power to detect modest persistence correlations (roughly r of 0.3 or larger is detectable at 80% power; r near 0.2 is not reliably detectable).
H2-H1 change is a noisy outcome derived from scoring, so a defense's share of it may be small relative to sampling noise and to pace, score-state and opponent-quality effects.
Selecting the best or worst defenses in one season and testing them in the next would be vulnerable to regression to the mean unless the test is pre-specified on held-out seasons.
Rule changes, roster turnover and coaching changes across 2022-23 to 2025-26 may make a team's defense non-stationary, which weakens the 'trait' interpretation.
uncertainties: No historical records were returned, so there is no evidence on effect sizes, reliability estimates or known failure modes.
The exact definition of H2-H1 (points per possession, margin, or score-state-adjusted) is not given in the task.
Whether the play-type graph and matchup-minute files are complete and consistent across seasons is unverified.
The effect of garbage time and late-game fouling on second-half scoring is unquantified.
The 2025-26 playoff data is labelled complete from 2026-06-21, but its handling in the analysis is not specified.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieval returned no records, so no earlier result was available to change the decision. The decision rests on the data description and on the sample-size and measurement considerations above.

blocking_constraints.text: 120 team-seasons, with about 90 year-over-year pairs, can detect only moderate persistence; small true reliabilities would be missed.
Opponent H2-H1 change per team may have low split-half reliability, so a null may reflect measurement noise rather than absence of a trait.

prior_work.summary: The retrieval returned no earlier study-family records, so it is unknown whether this question has been answered by this project. No prior work is relied on.

risks.text: Only 120 team-seasons (about 90 year-over-year pairs) limit power to detect modest reliability.
Split-half and year-over-year reliability of opponent H2-H1 change may be low, making a 'reliable trait' conclusion hard to reach either way.
Selecting extreme defenses in one season and testing them later inflates apparent persistence through regression to the mean.
Score state, pace, opponent quality, garbage time and lineup mix can move H2-H1 change independently of defense.
H2-H1 change is derived from the scoring outcome, so the defensive effect is entangled with the outcome definition unless possessions and shot quality are controlled.
Several H2-H1 definitions, halves and splits invite selection of the most favourable one.
Roster and coaching turnover and rule changes across 2022-23 to 2025-26 may break the assumption that a defense is a stable trait.
Using full-season or playoff information to define the defensive trait and then testing on the same games would leak the outcome into the predictor.

design.estimand: Intra-class reliability of team defensive effect on opponent H2-H1 change (points per 100 possessions allowed, opponent- and score-state-adjusted), estimated as year-over-year correlation of team effects and as split-half reliability within season.
design.unit: Team-season (defensive unit), with each game's second-half and first-half opponent scoring as the raw observations.
design.sample: Primary: NBA 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25 and 2025-26 regular seasons (120 team-seasons, complete data). Secondary and separate: playoffs, reported descriptively only. Exclude 2025-26 playoffs from the primary test.
design.power: Pre-specify a minimum detectable reliability of about r = 0.3 with about 90 year-over-year pairs (approximately 80% power at alpha 0.05, two-sided). Report bootstrap CIs; do not claim power for smaller r without a simulation.
design.controls: Adjust H2-H1 for opponent offensive quality, pace (possessions per half), score margin at halftime (garbage-time exclusion or win-probability window), home/away and starter-minute mix. Use possession-level rates, not raw points. Shrink team effects with empirical Bayes before any ranking.
design.falsification: Placebo outcome: H1 versus H1 split (first half of odd and even games) should show no reliable defensive effect. Permutation: shuffle team labels within season to obtain a null reliability distribution. A nonzero effect on the placebo outcome flags an artifact.
design.multiplicity: One pre-specified primary outcome (opponent H2-H1 points per 100 possessions, score-state adjusted) and one primary reliability statistic. Other H2-H1 definitions and split schemes are secondary with Holm correction.
design.decision_rule: Supported if the year-over-year correlation and within-season split-half reliability both have 95% CIs excluding 0 and the placebo effect is null. Rejected if the CI for the primary correlation is within roughly plus or minus 0.1 of 0 and the lower bound of a pre-specified equivalence margin is met. Otherwise uncertain. Any placebo effect or permutation-inconsistent result is classed as artifact.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files for 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular seasons, as complete at 2026-10-06 (2025-26 regular season complete from 2026-04-13); play-by-play, substitution intervals, starters, matchup minutes and box-score summaries; derived play-type graph used only after its consistency is checked against raw play-by-play; playoffs excluded from primary.
